To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipid X, MAGP, and IV-A are all capable of producing an acute pulmonary arterial vasoconstictor response.
the initial pulmonary arterial vasocontrictive activity of lipid X in the sheep is cyclooxygenase dependent and is mediated, at least in part, by the 3-hydroxymyristate moiety of lipid X.
lipid X and the disaccharide tetraacyl precursor of lipid A produce dose-dependent pulmonary hypertension that is blocked by prior administration of indometacin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pulmonary vascular responses to chemically defined lipid A precursor molecules.
the study of the effects of lipid A, a component of bacterial endotoxin, in sheep.
the study of the chemical and biological activities of the lipid X and MAGP molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lipid X is a precursor of E. coli LPS.
the pulmonary arterial pressor responses of the various monosacchride and disaccharides studied were all dose-dependent.
the pulmonary hypertension seen after the administration of lipid A and its precursors is due to the release of a prostaglandin from the lungs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monosacchardie precursors of endotoxin, such as lipid X and MAGP, are not as toxic as E. coli endotixin itself and that the pulmonary pressor response to lipid X may be mediated in part by the cyclooxygenase pathway.
the lipid X molecule is the minimal structure necessary to produce the early pulmonary arterial vasoconstictor response seen with endotoxin.
the lipid A precursor, lipid X, is the most potent pulmonary vasoconstrictor in the series of compounds we studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now identify and study the pulmonary vasoconstrictor activity of individual lipid X and MAGP molecules and their precursors.
lipid X and MAGP are toxic to the lung and may be involved in the pulmonary hypertension associated with sepsis.
